samples.summary: New dry-run branches in `docs get` and `tabs list` sit OUTSIDE the command's try/catch, so a throw from `getConfig`/`printDryRun` escapes the `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope
samples.evidence: docs.ts:125-128 and tabs.ts:14-17 place `if (opts.dryRun) { printDryRun(getConfig(opts), ...); return; }` before the `try {`. Every other dry-run branch added in this change (files.ts:113, notes.ts:82, slides.ts:87, api-keys.ts:34/52/72, docs.ts:78) is inside the try and therefore routed through `outputError` (which also sets `process.exitCode = 1`). `getConfig` -> `resolveConfig` -> `getConfigPath` -> `homedir()` / `migrateConfigIfNeeded` and `JSON.stringify` of a body are not guaranteed non-throwing; if any of them throws here the action promise rejects, producing an unhandled rejection / bare stack instead of the documented envelope and exit code. Low practical likelihood (loadProfile and loadSession both swallow their own errors), hence medium confidence, but the inconsistency is real.

samples.summary: Design doc states the `sheets cells get` range preview prints `?range=A1:C10`, but the implementation (and its new test) print the percent-encoded `?range=A1%3AC10`
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:849-851 says "the printed URL is the endpoint the range selects — `?range=A1:C10` for a range". cells.ts:26 builds `${base}?range=${encodeURIComponent(range)}`, and packages/cli/test/read-dry-run.test.ts asserts `.../cells?range=A1%3AC10`. The documented preview does not match what a user sees, which matters because the whole point of the section is that the preview is byte-identical to the real request.

samples.summary: `detectFormat` is now evaluated twice on the live path (once for pre-dry-run validation, once for the actual format)
samples.evidence: sheets-export.ts:42 calls `detectFormat(file, localOpts.fileFormat)` and discards the result purely to validate before the dry-run branch; line 64 calls it again for `fmt`. Harmless (the function is pure) but the discarded call reads like dead code; assigning it once and reusing at line 64 would be clearer.

finding.summary: New `seg()` guard is bypassed by the workspace identifier, which is still interpolated raw into every URL
finding.evidence: The change adds `seg()` for "every interpolated identifier" (http-client.ts:21-32), but `HttpClient.base` (line 98) builds `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${this.config.workspace}` with no encoding, and `listApiKeys` (397), `createApiKey` (404) and `revokeApiKey` (415) do the same for the management routes. `config.workspace` reaches the client straight from argv (`--workspace`, root.ts:66) or env/config file, so a value like `../../admin` or `ws-1?x=` retargets the same credentialed request the diff set out to protect — the exact failure mode described in the new doc comment, one segment earlier. `printDryRun` (dry-run.ts:30) interpolates it raw too, so the preview mirrors the mis-targeted URL rather than flagging it. The unit test only covers doc/tab/cell/key ids, not the workspace.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts `config.workspace` is interpolated raw into URLs, bypassing the new `seg()` helper. The code says otherwise at every cited location. `HttpClient.base` is `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${seg(this.config.workspace)}` (http-client.ts:100), and the three management routes all wrap it too: listApiKeys (http-client.ts:399), createApiKey (http-client.ts:406), revokeApiKey (http-client.ts:417, which also encodes `id`). `seg()` is `encodeURIComponent` (http-client.ts:32-34) and its doc comment explicitly names `config.workspace` as in scope (lines 28-30). The dry-run claim is equally wrong: printDryRun builds `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${seg(config.workspace)}${path}` (dry-run.ts:31, `seg` at dry-run.ts:12-14) and the api-key preview uses `seg(config.workspace)` (commands/api-keys.ts:16), so the preview matches the live URL. A `--workspace` value of `../../admin` or `ws-1?x=` is percent-encoded into one segment at all of these sites, so the described retargeting cannot occur. The reviewer's line numbers land on this exact code (off by ~2), so this is a misreading rather than a stale path. The only surviving sub-claim — that the unit test does not exercise the workspace — is test coverage, which is outside the correctness lane and not blocking by itself.
